title: Adaptive abort window and resumable-prefix checkpoints for interrupted streaming with tool calls
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: When clients disconnect mid-stream (especially during hybrid function/tool-call flows), partial generations and in-flight KV prefixes leave dangling state that either inflates cost (unbounded retries/prefetch) or silently loses useful prefix cache for resumption. Existing resume tokens are coarse-grained and do not capture function-call atomicity or soft-abort windows.

Goal: Implement an adaptive abort window plus resumable-prefix checkpoints that: (1) provide a short grace period to allow transient client reconnects without dropping ephemeral state; (2) capture compact resumable checkpoints that are safe to reuse across tool/function boundaries; (3) allow operators to tune urgency and memory trade-offs per-customer or per-route; (4) integrate with existing lease/heartbeat/eviction logic and fallbacks to cheaper model variants.

Scope:
- Runtime: checkpoint encoding, TTL semantics, and a compact resumable-prefix token format that includes function-call boundary markers.
- Orchestration: lease/epoch integration so checkpoints are retained during the abort window and can be garbage-collected after backoff thresholds.
- SDK/API: lightweight client signals (optional) to mark explicit abort vs network disconnect; backward-compatible resume token handshake for older clients.
- Observability: metrics and dashboards for checkpoint retention rate, abort-window hits, and cost delta.

Non-goals: full protocol redesign for all streaming modes, or strong consistency guarantees across multi-region failover in this ticket. Those are follow-ups.

Trade-offs considered:
- Longer abort windows increase memory and KV cache pressure vs reducing wasted re-generation. We choose adaptive windowing (short default, extended on recent reconnections and by customer tier).
- Checkpoint granularity: tokenizing by attention-prefix (small) vs full KV snapshot (large). We adopt compact prefix checkpoints with optional deeper snapshots for enterprise Dedicated deployments.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Add Checkpoint Manager component in the runtime that emits a compact checkpoint blob at function-call boundaries and on soft-commit tokens.
2) Implement Abort Window state machine: transient -> grace -> quarantined -> tombstoned. Integrate with existing lease/epoch tokens.
3) Extend resume token format (v2) to include: checkpoint_id, epoch, function_call_marker, checkpoint_ttl. Backward compatible fallback to v1 tokens that force fresh generation.
4) SDK: add optional client signal header (X-Stream-Abort: graceful) and a reconnection handshake that can present a resume token.
5) Garbage collection: hook into current sweep job; add cost-aware heuristics (LRU weighted by customer tier and recent reconnects).
6) Tests: unit (state transitions), integration (simulate intermittent disconnects + tool calls), perf (memory/latency under load).

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field for details.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New resume token v2 accepted by runtime and SDK; older clients gracefully fall back.
2) On simulated transient disconnects (50ms-3s) with function calls, at least 80% of reconnects resume without full re-generation.
3) Abort window transitions logged and metricized; dashboard shows checkpoint retention, eviction, and abort-window hit rate.
4) Memory overhead at 95th percentile increased by <8% for default abort window under standard benchmark.
5) GC correctly tombstones checkpoints after configured TTL and does not block unrelated sessions.
notes:
Initial design reviewed with runtime and SDK leads on 2026-03-05. Security reviewed scope: token format and KMS usage; decision to keep checkpoint blobs opaque (signed with service key) to minimize leakage. Enterprise option to store deeper snapshots in Dedicated using customer KMS.

Open questions:
- Exact default abort-window duration (proposal: 2s transient grace, 30s quarantined before tombstone) — requires further load testing.
- Per-tenant quota semantics for checkpoint retention.

Next steps:
- Spike to implement compact checkpoint blob (Miguel) — 3d.
- SDK handshake prototype (R&D) — 2d.
- E2E integration test harness to simulate tool-call heavy workloads — 5d.
- Small canary rollout behind rollout flag and metric gating.
